in_arabic.name: حرب
in_arabic.meaning: اسم يدل على الحرب والقتال في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: حرب هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه الحرب والقتال، وهو مشتق من الجذر اللغوي ح-ر-ب الذي يدل على المعنى نفسه. وقد ورد ذكر الحرب في القرآن الكريم في عدة آيات، منها قوله تعالى: 'وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا' (الإسراء: 36)، حيث يمكن ربط بعض المعاني بالحرب النفسية أو الحروب التي يجب مواجهتها في سبيل الحق.

in_urdu.name: حرب
in_urdu.meaning: نام جس کا مطلب ہے جنگ اور لڑائی
in_urdu.long_meaning: حرب ایک مذکر نام ہے جس کی اصل عربی ہے۔ اس کا مطلب جنگ اور لڑائی سے ہے، جو عربی جڑ ح-ر-ب سے ماخوذ ہے جو اسی معنی کی نشاندہی کرتی ہے۔ اسلامی تقویم اور تاریخ میں جنگوں کا ذکر ملتا ہے، جیسے غزات وغیرہ۔ نام حرب ان بچوں کے لیے منتخب کیا جاتا ہے جو بہادر اور جنگ میں ثابت قدم رہنے والے ہوں۔

in_hindi.name: हर्ब
in_hindi.meaning: हरब नाम जिसका अर्थ है युद्ध और लड़ाई

in_english.name: Harb
in_english.long_meaning: Harb is a masculine given name of Arabic origin. It means 'war' or 'struggle', derived from the Arabic root ح-ر-ب (ḥ-r-b), which conveys the sense of conflict or combat. In Islamic tradition, the term 'harb' is associated with battles and jihad. The name Harb signifies strength, courage, and resilience. Historically, it has been used in various Muslim cultures to denote someone who is fearless in the face of adversity.

historical_references.context: Harb Al-Khair was the name of a treaty signed between the Muslims and the Christians of Aylah (modern-day Aqaba). Muhammad, as part of his mission to expand the Muslim empire, led an army to conquer Aylah. The treaty allowed the Muslims to raid Christian ships in the Red Sea in exchange for leaving the Christian settlements alone. This event is significant as it marks the first instance of a formal treaty between Muslims and non-Muslims, setting a precedent for future interfaith relations.

historical_references.context: Harb ibn Umar was the governor of Egypt during the early Umayyad Caliphate. He is most famously remembered for his rebellion against Caliph Umar ibn Abdulaziz. Harb, who was a capable military leader, had been governoring Egypt for several years and was popular among the people. When Umar ibn Abdulaziz came to power, he wanted to reduce the influence of local governors and bring Egypt directly under his rule. Harb, who saw this as a threat to his power, rebelled and formed an alliance with various neighboring tribes. The rebellion was eventually put down, but it marked a significant challenge to the central authority of the Caliphate, demonstrating the complexities of managing a vast and diverse empire.
